entities.name: Titus Sextius Magius Lateranus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Titus Sextius Magius Lateranus, a scion of the distinguished Roman senatorial gens Sextia and ordinary consul in 197 CE, served during a tumultuous period of the Roman Empire, bridging the reign of Commodus with that of Septimius Severus. His career exemplifies the enduring power and political influence of the senatorial aristocracy, even as the empire transitioned into the Severan dynasty. The Sextii Laterani family, prominent from the mid-2nd century CE, maintained significant wealth and social standing, reflected in their ownership of the vast Domus Lateranorum on the Caelian Hill, which would achieve lasting historical significance.

Lateranus's most notable political achievement was his consulship in 197 CE, serving alongside Lucius Cuspius Rufinus. This appointment occurred during the initial consolidation of power by Emperor Septimius Severus, following his victory at the Battle of Lugdunum against Clodius Albinus. While the specific details of Lateranus's administrative contributions during his consulship are not extensively recorded, his elevation to this prestigious office indicates his continued standing within the Roman elite and his likely support, or at least acceptance, by the new Severan regime. His tenure would have involved presiding over the Senate, administering justice, and engaging in ceremonial duties crucial to the functioning of the Roman state.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Titus Sextius Magius Lateranus holds significance as a high-ranking Roman Senator and consul during a pivotal transition in imperial power, illustrating the continuity of aristocratic influence. His family's ancestral estate, the Domus Lateranorum, would later become the site of the Lateran Palace and Basilica, profoundly impacting the trajectory of Western Christianity.
